## Learning Objectives

By the end of this chapter, you will be able to:

- Inspect and understand data type schemas
- Perform type conversions using `cast()`
- Work with strings, numbers, and boolean operations
- Handle type-specific operations across different backends

Data types matter more than you think. The difference between a string and a numeric
type can make or break your analysis, and understanding how Ibis handles types across
different backends will save you hours of debugging.

## Working with Data Types

This example demonstrates how to inspect, convert, and work with different data types
in the World of Warcraft dataset:

```{python}
import ibis

# Load the World of Warcraft dataset
wowah = ibis.examples.wowah_data_raw.fetch()

# Inspect data types
print("Schema:")
print(wowah.schema())
```

This example shows how Ibis handles different data types: strings (with operations like
`upper()` and `lower()`), numeric values (with rounding and arithmetic), booleans (from
comparison operations), and type conversions using `cast()`. The `case()` statement
demonstrates conditional logic that returns string values based on numeric conditions.
